subject: Consolidated per-route telemetry and on-call UX proposal
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Tran <olivia@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated per-route telemetry and on-call UX proposal

Team —

Following our product/ops sync, I've sketched a proposal to improve per-route visibility in Console focused on three outcomes:

1) Accurate per-route cost and tail-latency breakdowns by tenant slice.
2) A lightweight on-call UX that surfaces offending routes and suggested next actions.
3) An agreement on sampling rates and the minimum telemetry we store at 30d vs 90d.

Attachments: per-route-telemetry-proposal.pdf, sampling-matrix.xlsx

Asks:
- Product: prioritize per-route view and a quick filter for SLO-violating routes.
- Infra/Serving: confirm feasibility for adding route_id tags at request ingress without perf regressions.
- Observability: propose default sampling tiers (1%, 10%, 100%) and a plan for dynamic bumping during incidents.

Can we get alignment by EOD Monday so we can slot a spike in vNext? —J

-- 
Jasmine Liu
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated per-route telemetry and on-call UX proposal

Thanks Jasmine—short questions:
- For cost attribution, do we need per-token accounting at the route level, or is per-response cost sufficient? Token-level could be costly.
- Are we expecting route_id to be customer-provided or generated at edge?

I like the on-call UX idea; would prefer an "owner" tag per route in Console. Also we should include a migration plan for existing endpoints.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated per-route telemetry and on-call UX proposal

Quick tech notes:
- Adding route_id tagging at ingress is doable; main cost is label cardinality in metrics and storage. We should limit high-cardinality metadata to traces only and keep metrics aggregate.
- KV cache effects: per-tenant cache hits can hide real latency; we need to surface both cached and uncached token latency.
- Proposed sampling: 0.5% baseline for large customers, 5% for mid, 20% for small until we have adaptive sampling.
- Created JIRA ticket: INF-1254 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1254) to track the infra spike and prototype schema.

Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated per-route telemetry and on-call UX proposal

Thanks for looping us in. This looks promising — two asks from ACME side:
1) Can we pilot with our top 10 routes (I'll send the list).
2) We need a sample export (CSV) of the per-route cost breakdown to integrate with our chargeback tool.

Happy to be in a quick call next week to walk through the UX. Let me know proposed timeline.
